wiki-iran.standing: The daily count of people reading the English Wikipedia article on Iran. It rises when the country is in the news, so the shape of the curve is a rough map of when the world's attention turned toward Tehran and what pulled it there.
wiki-iran.recent: Attention has drifted down roughly a third across the month even as the war ground on: the 60-day Islamabad MoU between Washington and Tehran lapsed on 17 August with nothing signed, and Israeli strikes in Lebanon killed 11 the same day. Hormuz transits fell to zero on Sunday, per Kpler data, while Trump threatened to bomb Oman, the mediator.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is priced against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: Brent sits near $93 after a rise off the Jul 2 low of $68.53, driven by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz: zero vessels transited on Sunday, Kpler data show, and Iran has legislated control of the waterway through a statute rather than a blockade. Adnoc is routing crude around it via Fujairah.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of US light sweet crude, the benchmark American oil is priced against and the one most US drivers eventually pay through. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and freight, plastics and fuel move after it.
wti.recent: The strip between May and July priced war risk out of the barrel, then back in: prices bottomed at $69.60 on Jul 6 before attacks put a premium back on. Two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting Hormuz, a third drone strike hit Libya's Zawiya refinery, and Ukrainian drones reached Nizhnekamsk, 1,600 km inside Russia.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a Louisiana pipeline hub and used to price most American gas contracts. It moves on weather, storage and production, and electricity bills, fertiliser and LNG export economics follow it.

wheat.standing: The world price of milling wheat, quoted per metric tonne, and the reference for bread and flour costs across importing countries. It moves on harvests, export bans and the safety of the sea and river routes grain travels on.
wheat.recent: Grain export infrastructure has been under attack while Europe dries out: Russia hit the rail station at the Danube port of Izmail on 14 August, days after setting Ukraine's largest Danube grain port ablaze, and drought has dropped the Rhine and the Danube low enough to shut a reactor at Cernavoda. The FAO price index reached 131.1.

rice.standing: The world price of milled rice, the staple calorie for more than half the planet. It is thinly traded and heavily policed by export bans, so a single government's decision can move what billions pay to eat.
rice.recent: Rice has fallen 17.7% over the window, to $464 a metric ton, well below the $563.8 peak of Aug 2024 and closer to the Oct 2025 low of $330.6 — a decline that runs against the wider food picture, with the Food and Agriculture Organization's price index at 131.1 and diesel at $5.36 a gallon feeding freight costs. The input does not explain the move.

copper.standing: The world price of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity. It is a proxy for building, wiring and grid expansion, and it is the export that funds several African and Andean economies.
copper.recent: Copper's climb to $13,540/mt has run alongside grid and electrification demand: Texas halted new data centre connections with 474 gigawatts of requests queued, five times peak demand. Supply has not kept pace — the Mes Aynak copper deal in Afghanistan, signed in 2008, has produced nothing.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt, the price at which the world's largest borrower funds itself for a decade. It is the reference rate under mortgages, corporate credit and emerging-market borrowing costs, so where it goes, the global cost of money follows.
us-10y.recent: The yield drifted up to a 4.75% high on Jul 31 and has held near 4.68% since, in a stretch where the dollar fell to its weakest since May as a rate hike was thrown into doubt and Trump again moved to fire Cook, reviving a fight over Fed independence. A weaker currency alongside higher yields is the market charging more to hold the debt.

sp500.standing: The main US equity benchmark, tracking 500 large listed companies and the reference point most American retirement savings and index funds are measured against. Inclusion in it forces passive funds to buy a stock outright.
sp500.recent: The index reached 7799 on Aug 13, its high over the period, and sits at 7745. Index membership itself moved individual names: Reddit rose 11% on an index committee's decision alone, ahead of S&P 500 inclusion set for August 18, while Jane Street took a $15 billion loss in July as AI stocks slumped.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index tracking the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange, weighted by market value. It is dominated by a handful of technology firms, so a move in one of them can pull the whole index — and much of the world's retirement savings — with it.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits near the top of its 61-day range after recovering from a Jul 29 low of 27190. Nvidia disclosed a $21 billion stake in SpaceX, a chipmaker holding equity in the companies buying its chips; Apple's China-only AI model cleared regulators in Beijing; and a judge faulted Google's Android install-flow remedy.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price American drivers pay for a gallon of gasoline at the pump, surveyed weekly across the country. It follows crude oil and refining capacity with a lag of a week or two, and it is the price most households feel first when either one is disrupted.
us-gas-retail.recent: Refineries have been the target rather than the oilfields: Ukraine said it hit two Russian refineries on 6 August, a drone attack on Nizhnekamsk killed at least 13 on 10 August, and a third drone strike set Libya's Zawiya refinery alight on 11 August. Pump prices still fell over the window, down about a tenth from the May 25 high of $4.475.

natgas-ttf.standing: The benchmark price of wholesale natural gas in Europe, set at a Dutch virtual trading hub. It is what industry, power stations and home heating ultimately pay for, and it moves on pipeline supply, LNG cargoes and how cold the winter is.
natgas-ttf.recent: The series has climbed roughly 47 percent from its December 2025 low of 9.46, reaching 17.93 in July 2026, its highest point in the window. The input does not identify what drove the rise.

vix.standing: A gauge of how much volatility options traders are pricing into the S&P 500 over the coming month, derived from index option premiums. It rises when investors pay up for protection, which is why it is read as a measure of fear in US equities.
vix.recent: Volatility has drained out of risk assets over the past three months, with the gauge down 18% from its June 10 high of 22.22 to 14.25 on August 14. The same calm showed up in crypto: Bitcoin's volatility nearly vanished as ETFs took in $754 million, while global equities hit record highs. India was the exception, with India VIX jumping 5% on August 10.

fx-pkr.standing: The exchange rate of Pakistan's rupee against the US dollar. Pakistan imports most of its fuel, edible oil and machinery in dollars, so the rate sets the domestic price of imported energy and food and the cost of servicing external debt.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee has been close to flat over the past month, trading in a narrow band between 278.2 on Jul 22 and 276.6 on Jul 31 to sit at 277.2. Nothing in the record explains a move of that size, because there was not one — the pressure showed up in prices rather than the rate, with diesel at 383.95 rupees a litre and gold at $4,392 an ounce.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate of Nigeria's currency against the US dollar. Nigeria imports most of its refined fuel and much of its food, so the naira's level sets domestic prices, and oil earnings in dollars are the main thing supporting it.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira firmed through the month to 1,352 per dollar on 18 August from 1,381 on 22 July, its strongest level in the window. Nothing in the period's Nigerian news explains the move: the run was dominated by the Osun election and its violence, and by scrutiny of oil revenue, including a $50 billion deep-offshore tax package.

fx-egp.standing: Egypt's currency against the US dollar. The country imports most of its wheat and fuel, so the rate sets domestic food and energy prices, and it is watched as a gauge of the state's foreign-currency position.
fx-egp.recent: The pound has been broadly stable over the past month, easing from 51.37 on Jul 25 to a low of 49.56 on Aug 8 and settling near 50.22. Nothing in the month's news explains the drift: Cairo's visible activity was diplomatic, hosting the Gaza roadmap talks and pressing its dispute with Ethiopia over the GERD.

fx-try.standing: The exchange rate of Turkey's currency against the US dollar, quoted as lira per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker lira. Turkey imports most of its energy in dollars, so the rate feeds straight into domestic prices.
fx-try.recent: The lira set a new 30-day low on Aug 18, drifting about 1.6% weaker over the month with no single break. The month's news was strategic rather than monetary: a defence pact signed in Mecca with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a law passed on PKK disarmament, and Moscow's complaint over US missiles reaching Ukraine via Turkey.

fx-bdt.standing: Bangladesh's currency, quoted as taka per US dollar. It prices the country's garment export earnings and its imports of fuel, food and machinery, and it is managed rather than freely floated, so its moves tend to come in steps.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka has drifted back to 122.5 per dollar after touching 124 on 7 August, a move of about half a percent across the month and no sharp break in either direction. The month's political news out of Dhaka — the government pressing Delhi over its stance ahead of Hasina's planned speech, and India's denial of involvement — did not register in the rate.

fx-idr.standing: The exchange rate of Indonesia's rupiah against the dollar, the price of Southeast Asia's largest economy. A commodity exporter with foreign-currency debt, Indonesia feels dollar strength in its import bill first, and the central bank in Jakarta manages the currency accordingly.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah firmed through the month, reaching 17,790 on Aug 17 after a high of 18,110 on Jul 28. The clearest domestic marker was Prabowo's nomination of a Bank Indonesia deputy as the central bank's new governor on Aug 11, on which the currency rose slightly. The magnitude-7.7 Flores earthquake that killed 53 left no visible mark on the rate.

fx-lbp.standing: Lebanon's currency against the dollar. It collapsed after the 2019 banking crisis and now sets the price of nearly everything in an import-dependent economy, so salaries, fuel and food track it directly.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound has been close to flat for a month, moving about 0.2% between its 31 July low and a 7 August high — the stability of a rate held at a fixed peg rather than a market finding a level. It has not moved on the Israeli strikes in south Lebanon that killed seven near Ansar on 15 August and eleven more on 17 August.

fx-cny.standing: The exchange rate of China's currency against the dollar, managed within a band the central bank sets each morning. It prices the world's largest exporter, so it moves the cost of everything China ships and the competitiveness of everyone it competes with.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan drifted to its 30-day strongest, 6.742 on Aug 17, as China's July data landed weak: retail sales rose just 0.6%, leaving Beijing's promised shift to household consumption undelivered and the surplus leaving as exports. Washington has accused China of evading tariffs, and Beijing has tightened drone exports.

fx-inr.standing: The exchange rate for India's currency against the US dollar, quoted as rupees per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker rupee. It sets the cost of India's oil and electronics imports and the value of remittances sent home by workers abroad.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee has firmed from its 96.5 low on Jul 24 to 95.67, helped by a softer oil import bill: India zeroed its windfall levy on fuel exports, cutting petrol's export tax from ₹3.5 to nil, and ordered 21 refiners onto state-set LPG quotas to close an import gap. Retail inflation edged up to 4.45% in July from 4.38% in June.

fx-brl.standing: The exchange rate of Brazil's currency against the US dollar, quoted as reais per dollar. Brazil is a top exporter of soy, iron ore, beef and coffee, and the real moves on commodity demand, domestic politics and the gap between Brazilian and US interest rates.
fx-brl.recent: The real weakened through the month, hitting 5.222 on Aug 15 against a low of 5.068 on Jul 23. Washington revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador on Aug 4, saying it would restore it only if Brasília accepted its own envoy pick — a diplomatic row with the country's largest trade counterpart.

fx-mxn.standing: The exchange rate between the Mexican peso and the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. Mexico sends most of its exports north, so the rate carries US trade policy, remittances and cross-border investment.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso strengthened to 17.05 from a 17.52 high on Jul 24, reaching its firmest level of the window on Aug 17. Washington's cancellation of Andrés Manuel López Beltrán's US visa and the $25 million bounty on a CJNG leader kept US-Mexico friction in view without denting the currency.

fx-eur.standing: The euro against the US dollar, quoted here as euros per dollar — the price of the world's second reserve currency. It sets the terms of trade for a bloc that imports most of its energy and exports machinery, and it transmits into every euro-denominated bond and invoice.
fx-eur.recent: The euro drifted to a 30-day low of 0.8633 on Aug 17, down about 1.1% from the Jul 26 high of 0.8792, on a run of domestic disruption rather than any single shock: jellyfish swarms shut three French nuclear reactors at Gravelines, and Brussels moved on a supply-chain sourcing law while Kallas prepared the autumn Russia sanctions package.

fx-jpy.standing: The exchange rate between Japan's currency and the US dollar, quoted as yen per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker yen. It sets the value of Japanese exporters' foreign earnings and drives one of the world's largest carry-trade flows.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen strengthened from 163.9 on Jul 26 to 156.5 on Aug 3 before easing back to 159.6. The weak yen has been flattering exporters: Toyota's quarterly profit nearly doubled to $9.4 billion. Regional security noise persisted, with North Korea firing a ballistic missile ahead of US-South Korea drills.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate of Russia's currency against the dollar, quoted as rubles per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker ruble. It tracks the country's export earnings, capital controls and war finances, and sets the price of every import Russians buy.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble weakened past 85 to the dollar as the EU prepared its broadest sanctions package yet, with Kaja Kallas claiming existing measures have cost Russia over €1 trillion. Ukrainian strikes reached deep into Russian territory, hitting the Samara rocket plant and a Wildberries depot near Moscow, while Russia says it downed 822 drones over Moscow in one night.

fx-zar.standing: The currency of South Africa, priced against the dollar, and the most heavily traded currency in Africa. It carries the country's mining exports and its politics, and moves on both commodity demand and the state of domestic institutions.
fx-zar.recent: The rand strengthened from 16.83 on 25 July to 16.15 on 8 August, its floor for the month, before settling at 16.17. The domestic news in this window ran to policing and procurement — soldiers deployed in Cape Town where 70 people were killed in a week, and the Prasa security-contract investigation in Pretoria — rather than to anything that would move the currency itself.

btc.standing: The price of one bitcoin, the oldest and largest cryptocurrency, quoted against the dollar around the clock. It has no issuer and no yield, so its price is set purely by what buyers will pay, and it sets the tone for every other crypto asset.
btc.recent: The month's peak came on 22 July, before a run of security failures and policy shocks: a Coldcard wallet exploit drained $120 million and congested the mempool, attackers emptied Lightning nodes at Foundation and Citadel21, and Russia banned bitcoin mining until 2032. Bitcoin sits 49% below its record while the S&P 500 hits all-time highs.

eth.standing: The second-largest cryptocurrency by market value, and the settlement asset for the network most stablecoins, tokenised assets and decentralised exchanges are built on. Its price moves with crypto risk appetite and with the rules written for it.
eth.recent: The price has drifted inside a narrow band, with a low of $1,845 on Aug 2 and no move larger than a few percent since. The regulatory calendar did most of the news: the Securities and Exchange Commission scrapped its Reg Crypto vote, the Senate's Clarity Act missed its pre-recess window, and the EU's MiCA migration deadline hit 10 million users.

paxg.standing: A gold-backed token whose price tracks a troy ounce of physical bullion held in vaults, giving crypto markets a round-the-clock proxy for the metal investors buy when they want a store of value outside currencies and government debt.
paxg.recent: Gold has climbed through a month of inflation-driven buying, with spot hitting $4,392 an ounce on Wednesday ahead of US inflation data — a ten-week high that the token tracked to $4,416 by 18 August. KPMG's first audit of Tether, which counted the issuer's gold bars by hand, underlined how much of crypto's reserve base now sits in the metal.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: Wikipedia's overview article on machine systems that perform tasks once requiring human judgment. Its daily readership is a rough gauge of how far the technology has pushed past specialists into general public attention.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Readership climbed to its high on Aug 14 alongside a run of stories about AI's spread into books, music and law: Amazon scanning and shredding rare books for training corpora, Spotify moving to stop promoting AI-tagged artists, and a Hartford filing that hid invisible text telling AI models to side with the plaintiff.

wiki-russia.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Russia — the world's largest country by land area, a nuclear-armed permanent member of the UN Security Council and a top exporter of oil, gas, wheat and fertiliser. Attention to it tracks war, sanctions and energy.
wiki-russia.recent: Readership climbed to its 30-day peak on 17 August, the day a Ukrainian missile attack killed six people in Koloskovo in Belgorod, among them a 14-year-old, and Kaja Kallas said the EU's autumn package would be its most far-reaching yet. The rise built through the week: Moscow said it downed 822 drones overnight, and Ukraine struck the Samara rocket plant.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Daily pageviews of the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking the country up, which tends to track the days it enters the global news cycle rather than anything happening inside its economy.
wiki-pakistan.recent: The late-July peak sits above a run of Pakistan stories that carried past it: the Mecca defence pact signed with Saudi Arabia and Turkey, described as a 'Sunni NATO' and now building a standing joint command, and fuel costs pushed up by war risk around Hormuz, with diesel reaching Rs390.42 a litre.

wiki-china.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on China — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking the country up, which rises when China is doing something that reaches beyond its own borders.
wiki-china.recent: Zhu Rongji, the former premier, died aged 97 on 12 August, prompting retrospectives on the reform era he ran; the peak on 13 August came alongside the US accusing China of evading tariffs. In the same window China's coast guard began routine patrols east of Taiwan, and July retail sales rose just 0.6%.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The 33-kilometre-wide sea lane between Iran and Oman through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil and much of its liquefied gas is shipped. It has no alternative at scale, so a threat to it reprices freight, insurance and fuel worldwide.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Traffic collapsed as the 60-day US-Iran MoU lapsed without a deal: zero vessels transited on Sunday, Kpler data show, after Iran passed a statute asserting control of the strait and the Guard Corps downed a US MQ-9 Reaper over Bandar Abbas. Trump then threatened to bomb Oman, the mediator, and a projectile hit a ship's engine room, killing one crew member.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The Wikipedia article on the 45th and 47th president of the United States, and one of the most-read biographies on the site. Its daily readership rises and falls with the news cycle around the American presidency, at home and abroad.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Readership has fallen roughly two-fifths across the month, from the 19 July peak to the 15 August low. The stories driving attention since have been foreign: Kushner's meetings with Hamas and Netanyahu to push the Gaza plan, the Hormuz talks with Iran and Oman, and the report that Trump left Ankara hidden inside a catering truck.

wiki-india.standing: Daily readership of Wikipedia's article on India, a proxy for how much of the world is looking up the country at once. It rises when something there breaks into general attention rather than tracking any economic or political measure.
wiki-india.recent: The 15 August peak fell on Independence Day, when Modi used the Red Fort address to promise eight more chip plants, nuclear expansion and free coaching for exam candidates, and an Army band opened the ceremony with Vande Mataram. Attention has drifted back since, through the Lakhisarai temple crush that killed six and Odisha flooding affecting about 515,000 people.

wiki-israel.standing: The daily count of people reading the English Wikipedia article on Israel. Attention series like this one rise when a country enters the news, so the shape of the curve is a rough map of which weeks the world was watching.
wiki-israel.recent: The 11 August peak came as Venezuela restored consular ties with Israel after 17 years, and as Ramallah reported more than 500 attacks on the West Bank in a week. Since then, Kushner met Hamas leader al-Hayya in Cairo to push Trump's Gaza plan, with Hamas demanding a withdrawal timetable.

wiki-ukraine.standing: The Wikipedia page-view count for Ukraine, a daily measure of how many people worldwide look the country up. It rises when the war forces itself back into general attention rather than staying inside the specialist press.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The rise tracks a fortnight of deep strikes and their costs: Russia set Ukraine's largest Danube grain port at Izmail ablaze, war-risk premiums closed Odessa's ports to shipping, and Russia says it downed 822 Ukrainian drones over Moscow overnight. Lavrov rejected freezing the war at today's front line.

wiki-nigeria.standing: The number of people reading Wikipedia's article on Nigeria each day. Africa's most populous country and largest oil producer, its politics and security travel far beyond its borders, and reader attention tends to follow the weeks it does.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Attention has drifted down from its late-July peak toward the 30-day low on Aug 14, even as the Osun state election drew crowds: civil society groups tallied 56 incidents and 14 deaths around the vote, and Adeleke's re-election drew congratulations from Atiku, Obi, Kwankwaso and Saraki.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Transits collapsed to zero on Sunday, Kpler data show, as war-risk insurance and owners' refusals closed the strait commercially rather than physically. An unknown projectile then hit a ship's engine room, killing one crew member, and Iran has moved to assert control by statute rather than blockade. Adnoc is routing crude around it via Fujairah.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Houthi fire has pushed the strait's daily crossings well below their 90-day baseline: a projectile sank the Indian-flagged MSV Faize Noore Oliya on 4 August, missiles and drones hit the Red Sea port of Mokha on 9 August, and six sailors died in a cargo-ship strike reported on 11 August. Maersk raised profit guidance to $6.5 billion on the rerouting.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic remains far below normal as attacks continue in the Red Sea: a projectile sank an Indian-flagged vessel on 4 August, and the death toll from a Houthi attack on a cargo ship rose to six. Maersk, which reroutes around the region, raised profit guidance to $6.5 billion.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic has held near its own 90-day baseline, down 2.1 percent over the last week, with no weather disruption. The strait has absorbed rather than lost trade: with Hormuz transits fallen to single digits, Malaysian refineries have seen Gulf crude arrivals drop, shifting supply toward longer routes that still funnel through Malacca.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic has run well below its own 90-day baseline as China's coast guard extended routine patrols to the Pacific waters east of Taiwan, and as Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy on that same eastern side. Typhoon Dolphin forced flight cancellations and evacuations in China in early August, briefly cutting movement further.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Traffic has fallen by roughly a quarter across the window, from 83 vessels a day on Jul 13 to 29 now, with the low of 22 on Jul 22. The input does not name a cause at the canal itself.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic has fallen through a Black Sea shipping war: TASS says Russia struck 130 ships since July, and Turkey has begun turning back some vessels bound for Novorossiysk on war-risk grounds. A drone killed a crewman on a coal-hauling tanker, and Ukraine struck the port of Novorossiysk itself on 12 August.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic runs about a fifth below its own 90-day baseline, with 112 vessels a day against a 163 peak on Jun 13. The strait's ferry corridor has been under strain since roughly 72,000 people crossed into Ceuta, a city of 84,000, and Spain and Italy began policing each other's borders. Seas were calm, with waves under a metre.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic sits at 168 vessels a day, about 2% below its 90-day baseline and well off the 210 recorded on May 23 — an ordinary summer drift rather than a disruption. Seas have been calm, with waves peaking at 0.6m. The Channel's news this month has been human rather than commercial: a dinghy carrying 157 people caught fire off Boulogne-sur-Mer on August 4.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Shipping traffic in Hormuz slowed to a near halt as the 60-day deadline for a US-Iran MoU expired, and a tanker reported explosions near Hormuz on 6 August; a sanctioned tanker leaking off Oman has spread a slick across 400 square kilometres. Traffic here sits 6.1% below its 90-day baseline, with rough seas and waves to 3.4m.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has fallen to zero, down 98% against its own 90-day baseline, after averaging 25 vessels a day in early June. The Black Sea has become a shooting gallery: TASS says Russia struck 130 ships since July, and Ukraine hit the Russian port of Novorossiysk in an overnight drone strike on 12 August. Grain and war-risk premiums move with it.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index sits below its Jun 16 high of 11150 after a run of Houthi strikes on Saudi territory: 12 missiles hit Yemen's oil provinces, a strike on Najran wounded 11, and Aramco put out a fire at its Jizan refinery, which processes 400,000 barrels of crude daily. The Mecca defence pact signed with Turkey and Pakistan on 7 August names no obligations.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index sits near the top of its 60-day range after a run of foreign-policy moves: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence pact in Mecca on 7 August, and parliament passed a law on Kurdish disarmament on 10 August. Against that, Moscow said a US arms transfer to Ukraine via Turkey undermines trust.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after a run that has outpaced the region's disruption. Seven blasts hit Jebel Ali port on 5 August and two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting Hormuz on 13 August, yet the Abu Dhabi-Dubai high-speed rail line broke ground and the UAE economy pivoted to expansion.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index has drifted down since its Aug 5 high of 1748 as the Hormuz closure worked through Malaysian refineries: Gulf crude arriving in the country has dropped and Hormuz vessel transits have fallen to a fraction of normal. The move is small — under 3% across the window — and the level, 1727, remains well above the Jul 1 low of 1657.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index sits near the low end of its two-month range, having fallen from 6,599 on May 18 to a trough of 5,342 on June 8 before recovering to 6,475. Prabowo's nomination of a central bank deputy as the new governor steadied the rupiah in mid-August, and an earthquake in Flores that killed 53 has cut Sikka's only coastal road.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index is roughly flat over three months, down 1.5%, having fallen to 22,670 on Jun 26 before recovering. July retail sales rose just 0.6% and industrial output growth slowed, leaving Beijing's promised consumption revival undelivered; Alibaba's $1.5 billion sale of Lingxi Games to Trustar Capital funds AI capex instead.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index sits below its May 19 high of 4170 after touching 3764 on Jul 17, with domestic demand the drag: retail sales rose just 0.6% in July, close to flat, against a household savings rate held up by a deflating property sector and thin pension and health cover. Alibaba's $1.5 billion sale of Lingxi Games to Trustar Capital lands into that market.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The index sits near the low end of a steep two-month slide, down about 8% over the window and troughing on Jul 30. Korea's memory makers carry the market: SK Hynix dropped 5% on a $38 billion fab bet, and all 2027 memory capacity is already sold out to AI buyers, with $880 billion riding on that wager. North Korea's missile tests ahead of US-South Korea drills ran through the same weeks.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index sits near the top of its 64-day range, having peaked at 78,950 on Aug 6 before easing. Policy moves ran through energy and payments: India zeroed its windfall levy on petrol exports on Aug 15, ordered 21 refiners to meet state-set cooking-gas quotas, and weighed ending zero-MDR digital payments that banks have subsidised.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index has climbed roughly a seventh over the past three months, reaching 5,754 on Aug 11 before easing to 5,722. Nothing in the window explains the run: the Singapore-datelined stories cover a hardware-wallet breach that leaked 39,798 buyers' addresses and steady Bab el-Mandeb shipping traffic, neither of which is an index-moving event.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index sits near the top of its 64-day range after bottoming at 39,930 on Jul 30, but has given up ground from its Jun 22 high of 47,740. China's coast guard now patrols east of Taiwan, the side where Hualien and Suao serve as the fallback if the Strait closes, and Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy in the same waters.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits near the top of its 44-day range after climbing from a May low, with the high on Jul 17 and a slip on the latest session. Thailand's political and security news — a school shooting in Nonthaburi and Bangkok's hosting of Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing — did not visibly move it.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after climbing from its late-May low, but fell sharply on the day. The drop came as the Senate impeachment court heard a former disbursing officer testify that Duterte ordered the release of P125 million in confidential funds to a security officer, extending testimony that earlier detailed disbursements with zero results.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after the RBA held rates steady on 11 August as the housing market softened, leaving another hike possible. The heavier drag is structural: China's steel stock is now old enough to recycle, and a shift towards scrap skips Australian iron ore.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index has drifted down about 0.7% over the two months, off the 117,500 high on Aug 7 and above the 108,300 low on Jul 23. Nothing in the record explains the move.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The index has drifted down through August, from 178,000 on Aug 3 to 166,900 on Aug 14, its low for the period. Washington revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador on Aug 4 and said it would restore it only if Brasília accepted its own envoy pick, leaving the diplomatic channel between the two governments unresolved.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index has drifted down through the summer to 64,250, its lowest of the window, from a high of 70,020 on May 27. Washington's revocation of Andrés Manuel López Beltrán's US visa on August 14 and the $25 million bounty on a CJNG leader kept the bilateral relationship strained, but the input does not tie either directly to the fall.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The index sits near 2,947,000, down 1.8% on the day and about 4.7% higher across the past 62 days. It peaked at 3,380,000 on 22 July and bottomed at 2,775,000 on 19 May. Nothing in the available material explains the recent move.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index sits near its high after climbing through the summer, with the peak on Aug 13 and a floor of 33740 back on May 19. The move is not explained by the Canadian news in view: wildfires that forced 20,000 evacuations in British Columbia, and the unresolved question of whether Canada avoids new U.S. tariffs.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index sits near its Aug 13 high after climbing about 5% over the past two months, and the input does not identify what drove the broad move. One visible mechanism: Reddit rose 11% on an index committee's decision alone, passive flows following S&P addition rather than any change in the business.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index reached 26,440 on Aug 14, up roughly nine percent over the window from its Jun 10 low near 24,200. Frankfurt's own corporate news ran through banking: Commerzbank said on Aug 6 that teaming up with UniCredit could create value, after Berlin had called the takeover a sovereignty threat. The coverage does not otherwise explain the climb.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The index climbed roughly 8% over the summer and touched 8,726 on Aug 10, easing slightly since. Two domestic shocks landed in that window: jellyfish swarms knocked 3.2 gigawatts of French nuclear power offline on Aug 11, and Western Europe recorded its hottest June and July on record, with heat derating the grid and the Seine running low.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index sits near the high of 1120 reached on Aug 13, up 10.05% over the window and little changed on the day at -0.158%. The input does not explain what drove the rise.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index has climbed about 13% across the window, reaching 20,210 on Aug 11 before easing to 20,160. Nothing in the material explains the rise; the Spanish news of the period was the eclipse crossing the country on August 12 and the Ceuta border crisis, neither of which is a market event.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range, up about 9% over the window and roughly a fifth of a percent below the 14,630 high set on Aug 10, after a low of 13,220 on Jun 3. The available material does not explain what drove the climb.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index climbed over the window to a high of 3327 on Aug 5, then drifted back to 3275. Neither the Volkswagen ownership dispute nor Spotify's move to stop promoting AI-tagged artists explains the index level itself.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.

wiki-turkey.standing: Wikipedia pageviews for the article on Turkey, a daily count of how many people looked the country up. It rises when Turkey enters a story people want background on — a treaty, a border, an election — and settles back when the story fades.
wiki-turkey.recent: Views peaked on 22 July and have drifted down since. The month's news was Turkey's alignment moves: a collective-defence pact signed with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan in Mecca, a law passed in Ankara on Kurdish disarmament, and rationed Bosphorus passage for vessels bound for Novorossiysk.

poly-us-iran-60-day-negotiation-period-e.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington and Tehran extend their 60-day memorandum of understanding. It pays out on the diplomatic calendar rather than on any battlefield or barrel, so it prices how much traders will stake on the talks channel staying open.
poly-us-iran-60-day-negotiation-period-e.recent: The contract collapsed from 75% on Aug 6 to 3% on Aug 18 as the 60-day MoU lapsed with nothing signed. Trump then threatened to bomb Oman, the mediator, and Israeli strikes in Lebanon killed 11 the same day. Hormuz recorded zero transits on Sunday.

xag.standing: A silver-backed digital token priced against a troy ounce of physical silver held in vault, so it tracks the silver price. Silver is both a monetary metal and an industrial input, which is why its price is more volatile than gold's.
xag.recent: The series moved from a low of 29.8 on Aug 6 to a high of 66.52 on Aug 15, and stands at 65.3. Nothing in the available material explains the move.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A prediction market on whether Vladimir Putin ceases to be Russia's president before the end of 2026. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, so it tracks how much money is willing to bet on the Kremlin's leadership changing hands.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: The odds drifted down from 9% in mid-July to 8%, with a low of 7% on Aug 16, while the war ground on rather than cracked: Lavrov rejected freezing the conflict at the current front line, and Russia said it downed 822 Ukrainian drones over Moscow in a single night. Deep strikes hit Russian soil without touching the Kremlin's grip.

wiki-venezuela.standing: Wikipedia's Venezuela article, and how many people open it each day. Attention to a country's reference page rises and falls with the events that put it in front of a general audience, which makes the count a rough gauge of who is paying attention.
wiki-venezuela.recent: Views have fallen by about two fifths from their 20 July peak as the post-Maduro story settled into procedural work: government and opposition closed a first round of talks on the courts and frozen funds, Venezuela restored consular ties with Israel after 17 years, and María Corina Machado hired a Republican lobbyist in Washington. The criminal economy did not fall with Maduro.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the US Federal Reserve raises its policy rate by a quarter point at its September meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on inflation prints, jobs data and anything touching the Fed's independence.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: The contract has drifted down through August, from 60% on 1 August to a low of 25% on 15 August and 28% now. The one Fed event in the window ran the other way: Trump again moved to fire Cook on 7 August, reviving the fight over Fed independence. Bitcoin traders were also looking past CPI to the Fed's next tests.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether U.S. forces will invade Iran before 2027. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with each escalation or opening in negotiations rather than with any official statement of intent.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Odds have fallen from 32% in mid-July toward the mid-teens as Washington's pressure has landed elsewhere: Trump threatened to bomb Oman, the mediator, not Iran, and Israeli strikes killed 11 in Lebanon. The 60-day MOU lapsed on 17 August without agreement, but the escalation showing up is economic — zero vessels transited Hormuz on Sunday.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the party that has held a parliamentary majority since the early 2000s, takes the most seats at the next State Duma election. It prices how firmly the governing party's electoral machine is expected to hold.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: Traders moved from 56 on Jul 19 to 74 on Aug 16 across a month in which the war stayed on Russian soil rather than moving toward settlement: Lavrov rejected freezing the fighting at the current front line, Ukrainian drones hit Samara's rocket plant and Moscow depots, and Russia says it downed 822 drones in one night.

poly-will-renan-santos-win-the-2026-braz.standing: A Polymarket contract on who wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election, priced in cents on the dollar for each named candidate. Traders buy and sell the outcome, so the number is what money will pay for a name, not a poll.
poly-will-renan-santos-win-the-2026-braz.recent: The contract has drifted down through the window, from 12% on Jul 25 to 4% on Aug 18 — roughly half its value over the month. Nothing in the coverage names a Brazilian campaign event behind the slide; the Polymarket stories here concern the venue rather than the race, including JPMorgan cutting the exchange off and a CFTC order overriding a state ban on prediction markets.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency whose ledger hides sender, receiver and amount by default, unlike Bitcoin's public chain. That privacy makes it the settlement asset of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the reason exchanges in several jurisdictions have delisted it.
xmr.recent: Monero climbed from its 20 July low to a fresh high on 18 August, and CoinDesk noted XMR outperforming while bitcoin and ether held steady. The month carried steady ransomware news: the FBI and South Korea warned of the Gunra gang targeting critical infrastructure, and a Ransom Cartel operator was sentenced in Washington to 16 years.

wiki-osun-state.standing: A state in south-western Nigeria, in the Yoruba heartland, with Osogbo as its capital. Its governorship elections are watched nationally as a test of party strength and of the electoral commission's conduct ahead of federal votes.
wiki-osun-state.recent: Osun voted for governor on 15 August, and Adeleke led the count by 67,232 votes after 15 of 30 areas before rivals congratulated him within a day. Civil society groups tallied 56 incidents and 14 deaths around the vote, and lawmakers have demanded a probe.

wiki-solar-eclipse.standing: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes between Earth and the Sun and casts its shadow on the surface. Totality — the Sun fully covered — is visible only along a narrow track a few dozen miles wide, so any given place waits centuries between them.
wiki-solar-eclipse.recent: The Moon's shadow crossed Greenland, Iceland and Spain on 12 August, Europe's first totality in 30 years, and readership peaked at 102,300 that day. Totality was brief along the path — 81 seconds at Teruel, under two minutes at Burgos — while Scotland's cloudy skies left eclipse hunters with mixed fortunes and the Channel Islands saw 90% coverage.
